_comment: Per-skill content guards — load-bearing markers that must survive customization. Each guard passes if ANY of its regexes matches the installed skill (Python re.search over the whole file, no flags — so `.` does not cross newlines and ^/$ are string anchors). Ported from sync.sh so the check outlives it; build-index.sh folds these into registry.json, and /skill uses them in `add` self-validation and `outdated`. WRITING A GUARD: bind the sentence that states the rule, not a word that happens to appear near it. Every alternate in an `anyOf` must be a rewording of the SAME sentence — never a neighbouring heading, table row, or output template, because those are exactly what survives when a customizing agent rewrites the rule. Validate by deleting ONLY the rule line and leaving the decoration intact: if the guard still matches, it is vacuous. An optional `note` field records why a non-obvious pattern is shaped the way it is; skill-lint and /skill read only `label` and `anyOf`.

agentic-audit.label: foreground-agent-batching
anyOf: [Dd]o NOT run agents in the background

agentic-audit.label: evidence-over-vagueness
anyOf: read surrounding code in changed files

autonomous-dev-flow.label: merge-report-entry
anyOf: entry in the final session report
flag each finished PR in the session report
autonomous-dev-flow.note: Merges must be accounted for in the report. Under the WITHHELD posture (see self-merge-posture) there are no merges and the 'Merged by this session' section is omitted by design, so the last two alternates carry the same obligation for flagged-not-merged PRs.

autonomous-dev-flow.label: self-merge-posture
autonomous-dev-flow.note: Critical Rule 5 is the single source of truth for whether this repo grants unattended self-merge, and every merge step defers to it. The alternates are anchor substrings taken from the two canonical wordings of that ONE rule: the first anchors the gated wording, the second the withheld wording, and the third is a fragment both skills' withheld wording shares (autonomous-dev-flow and tackle-issues phrase the rest of that sentence differently). None is redundant — dropping any one leaves a legitimate posture unmatched. The guard fires when the rule line is gone, not when a repo picks the other posture. Do NOT relax this to a bare 'Unattended Merge Gate' substring: that phrase also appears in prose about the gate and would pass a file whose rule 5 had been deleted.
anyOf: Merge only through the Unattended Merge Gate
NEVER merge, however clean the PR is
does not grant unattended merge authority

autonomous-dev-flow.label: explicit-path-staging
autonomous-dev-flow.note: Binds the SENTENCE that bans bulk staging, and binds it only if `-u` is still in the ban list. `-A` and `.` were already widely written down; `-u` is the one a customizing agent drops, because it reads as the safe flag (tracked files only) — and it is the one that corrupted a tracked .docx via the git-lfs filter (#163). A guard on `-A` alone would have passed the file that caused the incident, so every alternate requires `-u` to be named as prohibited. Deleting the ban sentence fires the guard; deleting only the surrounding `git add <specific-files>` line or the heading does not.

autonomous-dev-flow.label: lfs-filter-failure-mode
autonomous-dev-flow.note: Rewordings of the ONE sentence explaining WHY `git add -u` is banned: it restages tracked files a clean/smudge filter rewrote in the worktree, which turned a tracked 21KB .docx into a git-lfs pointer (#163). Guarded separately from explicit-path-staging because the rationale is what makes the rule survive: a customizing agent that keeps the ban but strips the reason leaves the next agent free to rationalise `-u` back in as 'the safe one'. Every alternate names either `-u`-is-not-safe, the filter, or the pointer.

autonomous-dev-flow.label: assert-branch-before-write
autonomous-dev-flow.note: Binds the re-verification rule, not the branch variable. `SESSION_BRANCH` is deliberately NOT an alternate: it appears in the bash blocks, so a guard on it would still pass after the rule sentence was deleted — vacuous. Alternate 2 requires a re-check verb on the same line as the command, so `BRANCH=$(git branch --show-current)` (the ordinary one-time read, e.g. create-pr step 1) does not satisfy it; the point of #163 is that reading the branch ONCE is exactly the failure.

tackle-issues.label: merge-step-routing
tackle-issues.note: Binds the MERGE STEP, not the word. Was `anyOf: ["batch-merge", "merge:off"]` — a bare substring that passed claude-code-notify, whose Phase 5 had been rewritten to `gh pr merge ${PR_NUM} --squash` (bypassing /batch-merge's Copilot gate) while two vestigial `/batch-merge` mentions survived in the Morning Summary template and Critical Rule 5. The replacement is scoped to the merge PHASE section — heading matching `#{2,4} Phase <n> …Merg…` up to the next heading — and requires `/batch-merge` inside it AND no executable `gh pr merge` inside it. `gh pr merge --auto` is exempted because the merge phase names it only to forbid it. `Phase \d+` in the anchor is deliberate: without it the summary's `### Merged by this session` table and the wave scan's `#### 2c. Check for User Merges` could stand in for the merge phase.

visual-brief.label: respects-reader-colour-scheme
visual-brief.note: #135: the skeleton shipped a hardcoded dark palette with no prefers-color-scheme query, so every brief rendered dark whatever the reader's system setting. Each alternate must match the CSS RULE BLOCK — the query plus its opening brace and :root — not the query string alone. Two earlier versions failed: listing the prose rules as alternates passed when only the query was deleted (anyOf matches ANY one), and matching the bare query still passed because Customization Points quotes '@media (prefers-color-scheme:light)' verbatim in backticks, so the guard matched the documentation instead of the code. Both partial mutants now fail. The two alternates are one claim in its two legitimate spellings: dark default with a light query, or light default with a dark one.
